solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thoroughly understood there is no danger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reply saying everything has been grasped
second meaning: the signal sounded when an air raid or threat has passed

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one sentence about grasping that a situation is safe, but each is a separate meaning of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used both to confirm full comprehension of instructions and as the siren signal that a raid or hazard has ended.

clue.text: Cause distress to Republican, on purpose

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another means it comes first, above the next

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Republican
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately upsets a member of the Republican party.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend the heart is to tear it figuratively, inflicting great emotional pain and anguish on someone.

clue.text: Wander in the mountains

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to roam over a wide area
second meaning: a chain of peaks

explanation.surface: A hiker roams freely among the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means roam freely; as a noun it names a connected line of hills or peaks.

clue.text: Give new meaning to stop sign, with ultimately severe penalty

parts.note: a red light tells traffic to halt

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the following word, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of severe
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: Running a red light is redefined as an offence carrying a harsh punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine something is to state its sense afresh, assigning it a different interpretation.

clue.text: Following, cross, into trap

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up enclosed inside it

parts.note: a net is used to trap animals
a cross is drawn as the letter X

explanation.surface: Afterwards, someone angry walks into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' in the surface; it is the shape X.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means coming immediately after in order or time, as in the following day.

clue.text: Trade fair certain to get publicity

parts.note: an expo is an exhibition or trade show
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Attending a trade show is a guaranteed way to get your product noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is attention from the media or public, the state of being widely seen and talked about.

clue.text: Made out pantomime figure

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recognised a character from a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, in which the comic older woman is traditionally played by a man in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: The dame is the stock comic female character of British pantomime, usually played by a male actor.

clue.text: Record-holder rolled up in warm weather?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cardboard cover a vinyl record is kept in

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun: the thing rolled up when it is warm
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the arm part of a shirt, pushed up when it is hot

explanation.surface: Someone holding a record finds it gets rolled up when the weather turns hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' suggests a champion athlete; it is the paper cover of a vinyl disc. The question mark flags the playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve is both the protective packaging of a gramophone disc and the part of a garment covering an arm.

clue.text: Picture gunmen surrounded by axes

indicators.note: something surrounded by other things sits in the middle of them

parts.note: the two axes of a graph are labelled x and y
the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

explanation.surface: A photograph of armed men encircled by people wielding hatchets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' suggests choppers but means the x and y axes of a graph. RA, the Royal Artillery, is the British army's gunnery regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray is a radiographic image of the inside of a body, a kind of medical photograph.

clue.text: A police check that gives crucial result

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun: something that yields a decisive outcome

parts.note: taken as written
the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detective branch
a test is a check

explanation.surface: A police inspection that produces a decisive outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from using acid to prove gold, so it is any decisive trial showing real worth or quality.

clue.text: Nothing by writer is publicly accessible

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces are set next to each other

parts.note: zero, shaped like the letter O
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Nothing an author produces is closed to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is available to all, with no restriction on who may enter or use it.

clue.text: Entertainer in revolt quits dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer in protest walks off by dancing out of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but belongs to the fodder: all thirteen letters of 'in revolt quits' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventriloquist is a stage performer who makes a dummy appear to speak, a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Having a number to deal with, king put out feeler

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: a king put out is ejected, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: to tackle a problem is to deal with it
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: With several tasks to handle, the king sent out a tentative inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out feeler' reads as a phrase about testing opinion; 'feeler' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentacle is a long flexible limb used by animals like octopuses for touching and grasping, so a feeler.

clue.text: Abroad as ever so horrible

indicators.note: something horrible is in a terrible state, so these letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being away in foreign parts is as dreadful as always.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe being in or going to a foreign country, especially one across the sea.

clue.text: Shines faintly, being hot, and cooks gently all round

indicators.note: cooking going all round something encircles it, holding it inside

parts.note: to simmer is to cook just below boiling
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Something hot glows softly as it is slowly heated through.
explanation.definitionFit: To shimmer is to give off a soft, wavering light, glimmering rather than blazing.

clue.text: On the border, welfare is a perk

parts.note: a fringe is an edge or border
state benefit is welfare payment

explanation.surface: Living on the edge of society, a person finds state handouts a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'benefit' is the everyday word for state welfare payments.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra advantage given to employees on top of salary, such as a company car, is a perk.

clue.text: In cell, a malign priest

indicators.note: in points to letters sitting inside the next words of the clue

parts.note: the run spans the end of cell, the word a, and the start of malign

explanation.surface: A wicked holy man sits in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma and the word 'a' are crossed by the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet, so a kind of priest.

clue.text: Answer people, having the last word

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
men are people

explanation.surface: Responding to people when you insist on having the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having the last word' looks like an idiom about winning an argument; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer or hymn, so it is literally the final utterance.

clue.text: Look determined: I'm expected at first to fall behind

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
set on something means determined
taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of expected

explanation.surface: Someone resolute says they are due to drop back.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or runner that loses time slips behind schedule, failing to keep pace.

clue.text: Den left impression

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an air is an outward impression or manner

explanation.surface: A hideout has left a lasting mark on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's hidden resting place, or a criminal's hideaway, is both a lair and a den.

clue.text: Pith helmet, best one

parts.note: top means best
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sun helmet is the finest one of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun hat made of pith, worn in hot colonial climates.

clue.text: Moorland is deadly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: high open hillside in northern England

explanation.surface: The open moors are a lethal place.
explanation.walkthrough: In the north of England, a fell is an upland moor or hill, as in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names high bare hill country; the old adjective means ruthless or lethal.

clue.text: Power in a simple electrical unit

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a mere thing is a simple one
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Electricity's strength comes down to one basic measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' looks like part of the electrical picture, but it only supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI base measure of electric current, so an electrical unit.

clue.text: United in love, we make money on the continent

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
U is the abbreviation for United, as in team names

explanation.surface: Joined together in affection, a couple prosper in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The continent' is the British term for mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the shared currency of most mainland European countries, so their cash.
